source_name: China Government Procurement Network (中国政府采购网)
authentication: none for the public search page; the search form displays a captcha field, which this task did not attempt to solve
rate_limits: UNKNOWN - not published; the probe used 2 requests at 0.9 s interval
licence: UNKNOWN - no explicit reuse licence found on the pages opened; treat as 'open web page, redistribution unclear'
update_frequency: daily (announcements are dated to the day; observed listing dated 2026.11.07-2026.11.09)
historical_coverage: not established - the search page defaults to a 7-day window; historical depth was not probed
entity_identifiers: 项目编号 (project number) - appears in the listing
no national supplier identifier in the listing
timestamp_fields: 公告发布时间 (announcement timestamp, e.g. '2026.11.07 18:24:08') - day+time precision
查询日期区间 (query date range) is a filter, not an event date
known_limitations: HTML only: there is no documented API. Any ingestion is scraping a public search result page, which is fragile and must be rate-limited and attributed.

The search form carries a captcha field. The keyword query used here returned results without it, but that cannot be relied on; solving captchas would violate the collection protocol and was not attempted.

Both annoucement types are mixed in one listing: 采购公告 (notice), 中标/成交公告 (award), 废标公告 (failed tender), 更正公告 (correction). Treating the listing as a notice feed would conflate tender publication with award.
No supplier identifier in the listing: winner names appear inside the announcement body text, so award->supplier links require per-notice page fetching and free-text parsing.
No device identifier; product/model text is inside free-text body content.
Chinese-language only, GBK/UTF-8 encoding variance across pages.
Only 2 requests were made; coverage claims beyond 'the search page answers' would be unsupported.
research_value: China is one of the five firms' home markets (Mindray) and a major public hospital buyer. Verified that the official portal's keyword search answers anonymous HTML requests with real, dated announcements, so Chinese public procurement is reachable - but only as scraped HTML with mixed notice/award types, so it is an exploratory source, not a reliable panel.
cost_notes: free public web access; no API, no key
